- tests/test_review_rb_judge_reissue_baseline.py:1-419 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The new pytest-based test file has no direct execution entry point and is not invoked by CI, so its regression cases never run.
  WHY: Running `python3 tests/test_review_rb_judge_reissue_baseline.py` does not execute the parametrized tests, leaving the baseline-resolver coverage inert; reviewers ranged from critical to CI-coverage concerns.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:343-477 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The resolver trusts only author-controlled issue-body fields plus a public PR lookup, so a crafted issue can spoof a valid baseline branch and metadata.
  WHY: Nothing binds the issue body to a producer-only artifact, so a hand-written issue can satisfy the branch-format and metadata checks and pass validation.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:361-364 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: `branch` is written to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` without escaping, so an `=` in the value would corrupt the output format if validation ever loosens.
  WHY: GitHub Actions parses `key=value` at the first `=`, so an unescaped branch would split the output incorrectly.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:393-410 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The metadata capture regex stops at blank lines, so a legitimate `Replaces:` line after a separator is missed and the resolver rejects the metadata.
  WHY: A blank line inside the `**Review-blocked reissue metadata**` block truncates the captured group, causing a false `metadata-missing` fallback.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:425-456 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The subprocess error handling is too narrow and lets other `subprocess`/argument errors escape instead of falling back cleanly.
  WHY: Only `OSError` and `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` are caught, so malformed `gh pr view` invocations can abort the step.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:387-406 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The regex literals are non-raw Python strings, which makes future regex escapes easy to mis-handle.
  WHY: Python can consume or warn on backslash escapes before the regex engine sees them, so later edits could silently change matching behavior or fail to parse.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:467-497 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The resolver verifies a PR head SHA prefix but still checks out the mutable branch name, leaving a force-push window between validation and checkout.
  WHY: `actions/checkout` resolves the branch tip at checkout time, so the workflow can start from a different commit than the one that was validated.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:513-519 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The ignored-baseline log message prints empty parentheses when status is unset, making the reason for the fallback ambiguous.
  WHY: Operators cannot tell from `Baseline override: ignored ()` whether the feature was disabled, skipped, or rejected.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
